'''Dame Polina Leopoldovna Bayvel''' ({{langx|ru|link=no|Полина Леопольдовна Байвель}}; born 14 April 1966)<ref name="who"/> is a British engineer and academic. She is currently Professor of Optical Communications & Networks in the Department of Electronic and [[Electrical Engineering]] at [[University College London]].<ref name="cf9c26">{{cite web |url= http://www.iop.org/news/17/jan/page_68718.html |title= Six IOP members are recognised in 2017 New Year Honours |publisher= Institute of Physics |access-date= 2017-01-03}}</ref> She has made major contributions to the investigation and design of high-[[bandwidth (computing)|bandwidth]] [[multiwavelength optical networking]].<ref name=frs/><ref name=ucl>{{cite web |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20160430225336/https://iris.ucl.ac.uk/iris/browse/profile?upi=PBAYV08 |archive-date= 2016-04-30 |url= https://iris.ucl.ac.uk/iris/browse/profile?upi=PBAYV08 |title= Prof Polina Bayvel |date= 2016 |publisher= University College London |location= London, England}}</ref>

==Education and early life==
Bayvel was born into a Jewish family,<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://hgss.org.uk/wp-content/uploads/2017/07/NL-April-2017-1.pdf |title=All The News From Hampsted Garden Suburb Synagogue |access-date=16 October 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171016070551/http://hgss.org.uk/wp-content/uploads/2017/07/NL-April-2017-1.pdf |archive-date=16 October 2017 |url-status=dead }}</ref> and grew up in [[Kharkiv]] and Leningrad (now [[Saint Petersburg|St. Petersburg]]) until 1978.<ref>{{cite news |title= "И 20 лет, и 30 лет – живым не верится, что живы…" – Общество |url= http://timeua.info/post/obshestvo/i-20-let-i-30-let---zhivym-ne-veritsya-chto-zhivy--00685.html |access-date= 2016-12-31 |work= Gazetya Vremya |date= 8 July 2015 |language= ru}}</ref> Her father is the physicist Leopold P. Bayvel, her mother Raisa (Rachel) was a textile/pattern technologist/garment engineer and later published studies in Eastern-European Jewish history.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Bayvel |first1=Rachel |title=Fifty Years On |journal=Jewish Quarterly |date=1 January 2003 |volume=50 |issue=1 |pages=56–58 |doi=10.1080/0449010X.2003.10703810 |doi-broken-date=12 July 2025 |url=https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/abs/10.1080/0449010X.2003.10703810}}</ref>

She was educated in England at [[Hasmonean High School|Hasmonean High School for Girls]]<ref name=who/> and University College London where she was awarded a [[Bachelor of Engineering]] degree in 1986 followed by a PhD in 1990.<ref name=phd>{{cite thesis |degree= PhD |first= Polina Leopoldovna |last=Bayvel |title= Stimulated Brillouin scattering in single mode optical fibre ring resonators  |publisher= University College London |year=1990 |url= http://catalogue.ulrls.lon.ac.uk/record=b1588357~S1 |oclc= 940321697|id={{copac|34556809}}}}</ref> In 1990, she was awarded a [[Royal Society]] [[Postdoctoral]] Exchange Fellowship in the Fibre Optics Laboratory at the {{ill|A. M. Prokhorov General Physics Institute|lt=General Physics Institute|ru|Институт общей физики имени А. М. Прохорова РАН}} of the [[Russian Academy of Sciences|Soviet Academy of Sciences]] in Moscow.<ref>{{cite book |last=Thompson |first= J.M.T. |title= Visions of the Future: Physics and Electronics |publisher= Cambridge University Press |isbn=978-05218-0538-4 |page= [https://archive.org/details/visionsoffuture00jmtt_0/page/208 208] |url= https://archive.org/details/visionsoffuture00jmtt_0 |url-access=registration |access-date= 2016-12-31 |language= en|date= 2001-07-02 }}</ref>

==Research and career==
Bayvel's research has focused on maximising the speed and capacity of [[optical fibre]] communication systems, and the fundamental studies of capacity-limiting optical [[nonlinear system|nonlinearities]] and their mitigation.<ref name=frs/><ref name=DuserBayvel2002>{{cite journal |last1= Duser |first1=M. |last2=Bayvel |first2=P. |title= Analysis of a dynamically wavelength-routed optical burst switched network architecture |journal= Journal of Lightwave Technology |volume=20 |issue=4 |year=2002 |pages= 574–585 |doi= 10.1109/50.996576|bibcode=2002JLwT...20..574D }}</ref><ref name=SavoryGavioli2007>{{cite journal |last1=Savory |first1=Seb J. |last2= Gavioli |first2= Giancarlo |last3=Killey |first3=Robert I. |last4=Bayvel |first4=Polina |title= Electronic compensation of chromatic dispersion using a digital coherent receiver |journal= Optics Express |volume=15 |issue=5 |year=2007 |pages=2120–6 |doi= 10.1364/OE.15.002120|pmid=19532448 |bibcode=2007OExpr..15.2120S |doi-access=free }}</ref><ref name=BaroniBayvel1997>{{cite journal |last1= Baroni |first1=S. |last2=Bayvel |first2=P. |title= Wavelength requirements in arbitrarily connected wavelength-routed optical networks |journal= Journal of Lightwave Technology |volume=15 |issue=2 |year=1997 |pages=242–251 |doi= 10.1109/50.554330|bibcode=1997JLwT...15..242B }}</ref> She has made major contributions to the investigation and design of high-bandwidth, multi-wavelength optical communication networks.<ref name= "6674f8">{{cite web |url= http://www.ucl.ac.uk/news/news-articles/0516/110516-royal-society-fellows |title= Three UCL scientists elected Fellows of the Royal Society |date= 11 May 2016 |publisher= University College London |access-date= 2016-05-11}}</ref>

She was one of the first to show the feasibility of using the wavelength domain for routing in optical networks over a range of distance- and time-scales. She has established the applicability of these new optical network architecture concepts, which have been widely implemented in commercial systems and networks. These systems and networks underpin the Internet, and the digital communications infrastructure – and are essential for its growth.<ref name=frs/> A new project, the Initiate project, aims to test technologies that will make internet connections faster and more secure, which Polina Bayvel indicated will allow them to test them at a national scale.<ref name="9dd986">{{cite web |url= http://www.urbanaworld.com/internet-playground-trials-new-tech-to-deliver-smart-cities/ |title= Internet 'playground' trials new tech to deliver smart cities |date= 14 February 2017 |publisher= Urbana World |access-date= 2017-02-14}}</ref> Her research has been funded by the [[Engineering and Physical Sciences Research Council|Engineering and Physical Sciences Research Council (EPSRC)]].<ref name=epsrc>{{cite web |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20160430225828/https://www.epsrc.ac.uk/about/people/polinabayvel/ |archive-date= 2016-04-30 |date= 2016 |url= https://www.epsrc.ac.uk/about/people/polinabayvel/ |publisher= epsrc.ac.uk |location= Swindon |title= Professor Polina Bayvel}}</ref>

==Awards and honours==
Bayvel won the [[Institute of Physics]] [[Clifford Paterson Medal and Prize]] in 2002. She was also elected a Fellow of the [[Royal Academy of Engineering]] in 2002 and was awarded the [[Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers|Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers (IEEE)]] Photonic Society Engineering Achievement Award in 2013. Bayvel was awarded an honorary Doctorate of Science degree in 2014 by the [[University of South Wales]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Honorary Awards 2014|url=https://www.southwales.ac.uk/about/our-organisation/honorary-fellows/honorary-awards-2014/#:~:text=Professor%20Polina%20Bayvel%20was%20awarded,her%20contribution%20to%20scientific%20research.|access-date=2020-08-17|website=southwales.ac.uk|language=en}}</ref> In 2014 she delivered the [[Clifford Paterson Lecture]]<ref name=patterson>{{YouTube|id=qezHUwou9dY|title=Communicating with Light: Clifford Paterson Lecture by Professor Polina Bayvel FREng}}</ref> and in 2015 was awarded the Royal Academy of Engineering Colin Campbell Mitchell Award.<ref name=frs/> She was elected a [[List of Fellows of the Royal Society elected in 2016|Fellow of the Royal Society (FRS) in 2016]].<ref name=frs>{{cite web |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20160429121052/https://royalsociety.org/people/polina-bayvel-12845/ |archive-date= 2016-04-29 |url= https://royalsociety.org/people/polina-bayvel-12845/ |publisher=[[Royal Society]] |location= London |title= Professor Polina Bayvel FREng FRS |author=Anon |year=2016}} One or more of the preceding sentences incorporates text from the royalsociety.org website where: {{blockquote|"All text published under the heading 'Biography' on Fellow profile pages is available under [[Creative Commons license|Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International License]]." --{{cite web |url= https://royalsociety.org/about-us/terms-conditions-policies/ |title=Royal Society Terms, conditions and policies |access-date= 2016-03-09 |url-status= bot: unknown |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20150925220834/https://royalsociety.org/about-us/terms-conditions-policies/ |archive-date=25 September 2015 }}}}</ref><ref name="6674f8"/> Bayvel was appointed [[Commander of the Order of the British Empire]] (CBE) in the [[2017 New Year Honours]] for services to engineering.<ref>{{London Gazette |issue= 61803 |date=31 December 2016 |page=N8 |supp=y}}</ref><ref name="53b573">{{cite web|url = https://www.gov.uk/government/news/new-years-honours-2017 | title = Press release: New Year's Honours 2017 | publisher = Government UK | access-date = 2016-12-30}}</ref>

In 2019, Bayvel was elected to the Board of Directors of [[The Optical Society]], serving a three-year term 2020–2022.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.novuslight.com/the-optical-society-elects-satoshi-kawata-as-2020-vice-president_N9636.html|title=The Optical Society Elects Satoshi Kawata as 2020 Vice President - Novus Light Today|website=novuslight.com|date=18 September 2019 |access-date=2019-09-18}}</ref>

In 2023, Bayvel was awarded the [[Royal Society]] [[Rumford Medal]] for pioneering contributions to the fundamental physics and nonlinear optics, enabling the realization of high capacity, broad bandwidth, multi-wavelength, optical communication systems that have underpinned the information technology revolution. She is the first woman to be awarded this medal since the medal was instituted in 1800.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://royalsociety.org/grants-schemes-awards/awards/rumford-medal/|title=Rumford Medal|website=royalsociety.org|access-date=2023-08-30}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Polina Bayvel has two sons.<ref name=spouse>{{cite web |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20160430220200/https://royalsociety.org/topics-policy/diversity-in-science/parent-carer-scientist/polina-bayvel/|title=Parent-Carer Scientist: Polina Bayvel |publisher= Royal Society |location= London |archive-date= 2016-04-30 |url= https://royalsociety.org/topics-policy/diversity-in-science/parent-carer-scientist/polina-bayvel }}</ref><ref name=tls>[https://www.bbc.co.uk/programmes/m000f5fz Polina Bayvel] on BBC Radio Four's ''[[The Life Scientific]]'' in February 2020</ref>
